pharm: Hydrolyzed collagen (collagen hydrolysate) is enzymatically broken down into low-molecular-weight peptides and free amino acids that are absorbed from the gut and provide substrate amino acids (notably glycine, proline, and hydroxyproline) plus small bioactive peptides used in connective-tissue (collagen) synthesis. It functions nutritionally as a source of protein/amino acids rather than as a pharmacologically active drug.

summary: Collagen peptide (hydrolyzed collagen / collagen hydrolysate) is a nutraceutical and dietary protein supplement, NOT an FDA-approved drug. It is widely used (including in India, often combined with vitamins and minerals) as a source of protein and amino acids for general nutritional support and for joint, skin, nail, and bone health. After ingestion it is digested like other dietary protein into peptides and amino acids that supply substrate (glycine, proline, hydroxyproline) for the body's own collagen synthesis. Typical oral dosing is about 10 g once daily, with reported ranges of roughly 2.5-15 g/day depending on the product and intended use. It is generally well tolerated. Efficacy claims for joint, skin, and bone benefits are based on limited supplement studies and should not be overstated; collagen peptides are not a treatment for any disease.

moa: Collagen peptides provide amino acids - particularly glycine, proline, and hydroxyproline - and small bioactive peptides that serve as substrate for collagen synthesis in connective tissue (skin, joints, tendons, bone matrix). When ingested, hydrolyzed collagen is digested into di-/tri-peptides and free amino acids, absorbed, and made available for endogenous protein and collagen biosynthesis. Some studies suggest collagen-derived peptides may also signal fibroblasts/chondrocytes to support extracellular matrix production, though this remains under investigation. There is no classic receptor-mediated drug mechanism; the effect is nutritional/substrate provision.

preg: Hydrolyzed collagen is a dietary protein and is likely safe in pregnancy when used in normal supplemental amounts; it is not an FDA-approved drug and high-quality pregnancy-specific data are lacking. As with any supplement, a pregnant patient should consult her clinician, and attention should be paid to any added vitamins/minerals and to product quality/source.
lact: Collagen peptide is a dietary protein and is likely safe during breastfeeding when used in normal supplemental amounts; specific lactation data are limited. Consult a clinician, and review any combined vitamins/minerals in the product.
renal: Collagen peptides add to overall dietary protein/nitrogen intake. In patients with significant renal impairment, where protein intake may need to be restricted, use with caution and under clinician guidance. No specific supplement dose adjustment is established because this is a dietary protein rather than a renally cleared drug.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is established; collagen peptides are handled as dietary protein and amino acids. Use within normal dietary protein recommendations.

minor: No clinically significant drug interactions are established for hydrolyzed collagen itself; review any vitamins/minerals added to combination products for their own interactions
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; it is itself a dietary protein and integrates with normal diet.
interactions.diagnostics: Not expected to interfere with laboratory tests; large protein/amino-acid loads could theoretically affect nitrogen-related parameters but this is not clinically significant at supplemental doses.

serious: Allergic/hypersensitivity reactions in individuals sensitive to the animal source (uncommon)
emergency: Signs of severe allergic reaction: difficulty breathing, swelling of face/lips/throat, widespread hives - seek emergency care

missed: If you miss a dose, simply take it when you remember, or skip it and take your next dose as usual. As a dietary supplement, there is no need to double up to make up for a missed dose.
overdose: Overdose in the medical sense is not expected; collagen peptide is a dietary protein. Taking unusually large amounts may cause gastrointestinal discomfort such as bloating, fullness, or a feeling of heaviness. Management is supportive. Excessive total protein intake is generally undesirable in significant renal impairment.
